perspective:
From my perspective as Arthur Chung, the information available to me is:

- I am Arthur Chung, a doctorate-holding plumber. I know Teresa Ortega as a colleague/collaborator on community service projects.
- I noticed Teresa working hard and appearing overwhelmed. I felt concerned and believed she needed help, so I offered assistance. Teresa said it was kind but she thought she could manage, though there was a lot to do. I said self-care mattered and offered to help; she accepted help organizing medical supplies, and we started.
- I believed she was hesitant because she wanted to prove her capability. I empathized with her self-reliance and reassured her that accepting help did not mean she was not capable. Teresa said she appreciated it and wanted to show she could do it herself. I said teamwork can be more effective and it is about getting the job done; she agreed she needed to remind herself. I said we were in it together and I was there to support her.
- I believed she was still struggling. I felt frustrated that my help was not yielding results and wanted another way to support her without making her feel inadequate. I told her I could see things were still tough and that she was doing a great job. Teresa said it had been busy and she felt behind. I suggested working together instead of just me helping; she agreed, and we decided to tackle it as a team.
- I felt hopeful that collaboration would ease her burden and improve efficiency, and I committed to it. I told her I was hopeful. Teresa said it already felt less overwhelming. I proposed I handle inventory while she managed patient records, with regular check-ins. She agreed and was glad; I was too.
- I believed our collaboration strengthened our professional relationship and felt satisfied. I said our teamwork paid off and we accomplished more together. Teresa agreed and said it was a great experience. I suggested continuing collaboration in future projects; she called it a fantastic idea and said we proved we can be more efficient/effective as a team. I said we should keep it up and I looked forward to our next project. Teresa thanked me for being supportive.
